audit.title: CCIP Best Practices (Aptos)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Sections open with the answer: "Before calling the `router::ccip_send` entry function, your application should verify that the destination chain is supported." Question-headings are answered in their first sentence. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. 24 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, zero level skips, median 52 words/section. Weak spot: 0 tables — the account-type decision and `gasLimit` rules are prose/bullets where a table would extract better.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Only 3 prose numerals (2 per 1k words), 0 with units, no version strings; `gasLimit` of `0` is the sole concrete value. "Soak test" and service-limit sections reference limits without naming any numbers.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 7 links, 0 to primary sources; external links are contact/terms pages, not Aptos SDK docs, Move specs, or the CCIP architecture reference.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. Liftable statements like "The CCIP `ReceiverRegistry` is designed to map a single account address to a single, unique `ccip_receive` function" are self-contained.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Poor. No JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified`/`datePublished` in head, no og/twitter tags. Body carries "Last Updated: 2025-09-03" but it is not machine-exposed.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Mixed. 3 tagged blocks, but rust snippets omit imports/module scaffolding, `E_UNTRUSTED_SOURCE_CHAIN` and `E_UNTRUSTED_SENDER` are used but never defined, and one block relies on placeholder comments ("// Your allowlist logic").

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good. Full lifecycle (verify → decouple → deploy → soak test → monitor → audit) and question-phrased headings. Gap: no error-string / symptom coverage (e.g., what failure looks like when sending to an unsupported chain).

audit.summary: This is a well-structured, cleanly written best-practices guide for building CCIP receivers on Aptos, and its biggest strength is retrieval-friendly chunking: 24 small sections, several phrased as the exact questions developers ask ("Why must `ccip_receive` fetch its own data payload?"). The biggest opportunity is machine-readability and specificity — the page ships with zero JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no head-level dates, almost no quantitative detail, and no primary-source citations. The honest verdict: strong bones, but under-instrumented for generative retrieval and thin on the concrete numbers and authoritative links that lift citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and machine-readable dates
recommendations.issue: "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)… canonical: MISSING… datePublished absent / dateModified absent"
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-09-03`, `inLanguage: en`, `programmingLanguage: [Move, TypeScript]`, and add `<link rel="canonical">`.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness signals raise agent trust/E-E-A-T and parseability.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom/troubleshooting section with error strings
recommendations.where: new H2 near "Verify destination chain" / end of page
recommendations.issue: No content matches symptom queries like "CCIP send fails to unsupported chain" or the `E_UNTRUSTED_SOURCE_CHAIN` abort.
recommendations.change: Add a short "Common errors" section mapping each abort code (`E_UNTRUSTED_SOURCE_CHAIN`, `E_UNTRUSTED_SENDER`) and the unsupported-chain revert to cause + fix.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by error text; symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept prose loses.

recommendations.title: Cite primary sources inline
recommendations.where: "Verify destination chain", "Key Concepts for Aptos Receivers"
recommendations.issue: "0 to primary sources"; only contact/terms links present.
recommendations.change: Link `@aptos-labs/ts-sdk` to its package/docs, `receiver_registry`/`ReceiverRegistry` to the CCIP Move module reference, and resource accounts to the Aptos resource-account docs.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Convert the account-type decision to a comparison table
recommendations.where: "When must a receiver module be deployed under a Resource Account?"
recommendations.issue: Decision logic (resource vs user vs code object) is buried in two bullets.
recommendations.change: Add a 3-row table: Account type | Handles tokens? | Signer capability | Recommended when.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract explicit reasons and build justified answers.

recommendations.title: Complete the Move snippets
recommendations.issue: Undefined `E_UNTRUSTED_SOURCE_CHAIN`/`E_UNTRUSTED_SENDER`; missing `module`/`use` scaffolding; placeholder `// Your allowlist logic`.
recommendations.change: Add `const E_UNTRUSTED_SOURCE_CHAIN: u64 = 1;` declarations, wrap snippets in a minimal `module` with `use` imports, and show a concrete `is_allowed_source_chain` stub.
recommendations.why: Copy-pasteable, self-contained code is preferred by coding agents and cited more.

recommendations.title: Add concrete numbers to limits/testing guidance
recommendations.issue: "Be aware of the Service Limits and Rate Limits" with no figures; vague "several".
recommendations.change: Cite the specific rate-limit/finality values (or link the exact directory row) and state why `allow_out_of_order_execution` must be `true` on Aptos (finality/ordering model).
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes for source visibility.

recommendations.title: Lead the `extraArgs` section with the canonical Aptos requirement
recommendations.issue: The mandatory `allow_out_of_order_execution: true` rule appears only in a CAUTION box after general prose.
recommendations.change: Put "On Aptos you **must** set `allow_out_of_order_execution` to `true` (source or destination)" as the section's first liftable sentence; name hardcoding `extra_args` as an explicit Don't.
recommendations.why: Answer-first canonical facts defend against skims and generic-EVM priors.

antiPatterns: Undefined identifiers in code (`E_UNTRUSTED_SOURCE_CHAIN`, `E_UNTRUSTED_SENDER`) and placeholder comments reduce runnability.
One vague quantifier ("several") where a count would serve.
Freshness date present in body but not machine-exposed in head.
No walls of prose, no keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff — clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is referenced at top — good; ensure it lists this URL.
JSON-LD/canonical/og tags are template-level fixes across `docs.chain.link`, not just this page; CLI should pass raw `<head>` next run to confirm absence vs non-capture.
Primary-source authority (Aptos SDK, Move module refs) partly depends on those targets being canonical, stable URLs.
